g.text: Level Curves, Two-Path Limit Test, Total Differential df, Chain Rule Tree, Implicit Differentiation & Euler Theorems
Surfaces z = f(x, y) & Level Curves (Contours)
Level curve is the 2D projection of surface slice at height z = k: f(x, y) = k
Level curves x² + y² = k are concentric CIRCLES.
Gradient ∇f = [2x, 2y]ᵀ is perpendicular to level curve!
Level curves x² - y² = k are HYPERBOLAS.
k = 0 gives pair of intersecting lines y = ±x (saddle!).
If f(x, y) approaches different values along two distinct approach paths to (x₀, y₀), the LIMIT DOES NOT EXIST!
= lim_{x➔0} m x² / [x²(1 + m²)] = m / (1 + m²)
DEPENDS ON SLOPE m ⟹ LIMIT DOES NOT EXIST!
Parabolic Trap Path: y = kx² (Degree Matching)
Along y = mx: limit = 0 for all straight lines!
Along y = x²: limit = x⁴/(2x⁴) = 1/2 ≠ 0 ⟹ LIMIT DNE!
EXAM SAFEGUARD: Always balance polynomial degrees! If denominator has x⁴ + y², straight lines give false 0; test y = kx²!
Δf / f ≈ (1/f) • (∂f/∂x) Δx + (1/f) • (∂f/∂y) Δy ⟹ Percentage Error = (Δf / f) × 100%
z = f(x, y) where x = x(t), y = y(t):

Saves massive algebra compared to implicit product rules!
Definition: Homogeneous Function of Degree n
f(x, y) is homogeneous of degree n if: f(tx, ty) = tⁿ • f(x, y) for all t > 0
Alternatively: f(x, y) = xⁿ • g(y/x) = yⁿ • h(x/y)
Example: f(x, y) = (x³ + y³) / (x + y) has degree n = 3 - 1 = 2.
For homogeneous function f(x, y) of degree n:
For 3 variables: x f_x + y f_y + z f_z = n • f(x, y, z)
Second-order differential operator of degree n:
x² f_xx + 2xy f_xy + y² f_yy = n(n - 1) • f
Matrix form: [x y] • H_f • [x y]ᵀ = n(n - 1) f
TRAP: If n = 1, second-order operator vanishes to 0!
COMPOSITE EULER THEOREM • THE MOST FAMOUS GATE QUESTION TYPE
Problem Archetype: When u(x, y) is NOT homogeneous, but g(u) = f(x, y) IS homogeneous of degree n!
E.g. u = sin⁻¹[(x² + y²)/(x + y)] ⟹ sin(u) = (x² + y²)/(x + y) which is homogeneous of degree n = 2 - 1 = 1.
x u_x + y u_y = n • [ g(u) / g'(u) ]
x² u_xx + 2xy u_xy + y² u_yy = G(u)[G'(u) - 1]
RAPID EXAM LOOKUP TABLE FOR g(u)/g'(u):
• u = sin⁻¹(f) ⟹ g/g' = sin u / cos u = tan u
x u_x + y u_y = (1/2) tan u
• g/g' = tan u / sec² u = (1/2) sin 2u
